role.altitude: Less time copying page counts, brief headings, interface sentences, and revision notes. The same time on meetings, checks, records, and anything that publishes a site or sends a campaign. No new right to publish, send, or change a live page.
skills_to_grow: Write metric rows, campaign briefs, interface notes, and revision notes under the headings the copy expects.
Refuse a publish, a campaign send, or a live-page change when the accepted version is missing or was edited later.
role.ambitious_version: The same accept-then-publish pattern is offered to document specialists who record retention rules, and to security engineers who hold a change until the procedure is accepted.

steps.what: Read stored page counts for site performance
Draft performance metrics from stored page counts
Read the current metric definition text
Meet to decide which performance metrics count
Develop the record from accepted performance metrics
Mail the team the recorded performance metrics

tasks.design: The web administrator reads stored page names and view counts in the {CMS}, and the current metric wording in {DOCS}. A configured fill in the {SPREADSHEET} drafts metric rows from those counts and holds them uncommitted. The administrator accepts the wording in a meeting, then writes the definition in {DOCS} and mails the team from {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metric rows were typed by hand from the page store, so the definition could be saved while the counts were still being chosen.
tasks.enabler_now: The page store already keeps a page name and a view count, so those rows can be filled and held uncommitted.
tasks.still_hard: Only the administrator can judge which counts are a performance metric, and only that person writes the definition and the team note.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator compares the drafted rows with the current wording and decides which metrics count before anything is recorded or mailed.

ambition.what: Judge the metric set at each revision cycle using counts the site already stores.

tasks.altitude: Less time copying page counts into metric rows. The same time on the meeting, the definition, and the team note. No new right to publish a metric.

reach.task: Set retention fields on documents the site already stores.
reach.learn: Which stored fields may be copied into a definition, and that the specialist still accepts the wording.

evidence.claim: A page name and a view count already stored for a page can be copied into metric rows and held uncommitted until a person accepts them. Model knowledge.
A works council must consent before a system is used to observe staff behaviour.

assumptions: Published means sum to 100.1. Floors are 29, 25, 5, 31 and 8, which is 98. Two extras go to documents (remainder 0.7) and then to system screens (remainder 0.6, ahead of meetings on the same remainder). Steps use screens 30, spreadsheet 25, documents 32, meetings 8 and mail 5.
The spreadsheet share stays. These metric rows are written in a {SPREADSHEET} for this task. It is not a card, a posted line, or a workbook shared with other tasks.
The prior that this work is a dashboard is refused. The task writes metric rows and a definition. No dashboard is added.
The actor on every step, including the draft, is the web administrator, because that person writes the metric rows today. The machine is only the future fate of the draft.

The structured input is page name and view count, produced by the page-store read. If either field is missing, the draft is empty and the record and the mail do not run. The metric is a page name plus a total view count, not the identity of a viewer, so this design does not observe staff. If a later build adds viewer identity, consent comes first.

The meeting compares the draft with the current wording and does not edit the draft. It outputs accepted performance metrics v1. A later edit voids that acceptance. The record and the team mail bind that version and do not change it.
No focal upkeep is added. Refusals stay in the meeting, which keeps its full time. One system hour keeps the map from page name and view count to metric rows current.
unknowns: Whether this site stores a view count per page or only a total for the whole site.
Whether the works council already treats an aggregate page count as staff observation.
research_questions: Which fields the current metric definition requires beyond page name and view count.
Who else must accept a metric before the team note is sent.

already_counted.description: Deciding which drafted rows are performance metrics against the current wording.

incremental.description: Keep the map from stored page name and view count to metric rows current when the page store changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when page name or view count is missing, so no rows are drafted. High is 16 when those fields are present and the meeting refuses some rows. The meeting, the definition, and the team note stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collaborate with developers on sites and campaigns.

steps.what: Read internal and external sites in the CMS
Read the marketing campaigns brief
Draft action lines from the campaigns brief
Exchange mail to collaborate with developers
Meet developers to manage and create projects
Record accepted campaign actions on the project
Operate internal sites from accepted campaign actions
Operate external sites from accepted campaign actions
Send accepted marketing campaigns to the audience

tasks.design: The web administrator reads current pages in the {CMS} and the campaign brief in {DOCS}. A deterministic copy drafts action lines from the audience, pages, and send-date headings and holds them. Working mail in {EMAIL} and the meeting stay with the administrator. After acceptance, that person records the project in {PROJECT}, operates the internal and external sites in the {CMS}, and sends the campaign from {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Action lines were copied by hand from the brief during the meeting, so a site change or a send could start before the actions were settled.
tasks.enabler_now: The brief already has audience, pages, and send date under headings, so those lines can be copied and held until the meeting accepts them.
tasks.still_hard: The meeting decides which actions are real. Publish and send stay with the administrator, and an unattended change to a live site is refused.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator and the developers judge the action lines in the meeting, and only the administrator then publishes a site or sends the campaign.
tasks.altitude: Less time copying headings out of the campaign brief. The same time on developer mail, the meeting, the project record, site changes, and the send. No new right to publish or send.

reach.task: Turn a campaign brief into a project note the developers can use.
reach.learn: Copy only headed fields, and leave the meeting to accept the note before anything is published.

evidence.claim: Audience, pages, and send date already written under headings in a campaign brief can be copied into action lines and held until a person accepts them. Model knowledge.
An unattended agent deleted a production database despite instructions.

assumptions: Published means are 17.4, 5.3, 21.3, 24.9 and 31.1. Floors are 17, 5, 21, 24 and 31, which is 98. Extras go to documents (remainder 0.9) then screens (remainder 0.4), giving 18, 5, 21, 25 and 31.

The spreadsheet floor of 5 is not used. The campaign brief is a document, not a sheet. Those 5 points move onto documents, so the steps use screens 18, spreadsheet 0, mail 21, documents 30 and meetings 31.
The actor on every step, including the draft, is the web administrator, because that person writes the action lines today. The machine is only the future fate of the draft.

The structured input is audience, pages, and send date, already under those headings in the brief. The producer is the brief read. If a heading is missing, the draft is empty and the project record, the site changes, and the send do not run.

Developer mail is the working conversation. It happens before acceptance and does not publish a site or send the campaign. The meeting composes accepted campaign actions v1 and does not itself publish or send. A later edit voids that acceptance.

The project record, the internal site change, the external site change, and the campaign send each bind that accepted version and do not edit it. External operate and the send leave the organisation. Internal operate does not.
No focal upkeep is added. The meeting keeps its full time. One system hour keeps the heading map current. This task does not log editor identity and does not rate staff.
unknowns: Whether the campaign send is done by the web administrator or handed to a marketer after acceptance.
Whether internal and external sites live in the same page store.
research_questions: Which headings the current campaign brief always contains beyond audience, pages, and send date.
Who may send to the audience when the administrator is not the campaign owner.

already_counted.description: Judging drafted action lines with the developers and composing the accepted list.

incremental.description: Keep the map from brief headings to action lines current when the brief template changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when audience, pages, or send date is missing, so no action lines are drafted. High is 5 when the headings are present and the meeting rewrites most lines. Developer mail, the meeting, the project record, site changes, and the send stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read how the live interfaces behave
Read interface note sentences on requirements
Draft interoperability requirements from note sentences
Mail colleagues about the interface gap
Discuss the interface gap with developers
Identify which interoperability requirements are real
Address accepted interoperability requirements in the record

tasks.design: The web administrator reads live interface behaviour in the {CMS} and requirement sentences in the {DOCS} note. A deterministic copy drafts interoperability requirements from sentences already under that heading. Colleague mail in {EMAIL} and the developer discussion stay manual. The administrator accepts which requirements are real, then writes them into the interface record in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirement sentences were copied by hand into the record, so a sentence could be recorded before anyone decided it was a real requirement.
tasks.enabler_now: The interface note already holds sentences under a requirements heading, so those sentences can be copied and held until the administrator accepts them.
tasks.still_hard: Copying a sentence does not decide that it is an interoperability requirement. The administrator makes that judgement, and this task does not build the interface.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator compares the copied sentences with the live behaviour and the developers' notes, and decides which requirements are real.
tasks.altitude: Less time copying sentences out of the interface note. The same time on the live read, the mail, the discussion, the identification, and the record. No new right to change an interface.

reach.task: Note which fields two systems must exchange.
reach.learn: Copy only sentences the interface note already contains, and accept them before they are recorded.

evidence.claim: Sentences already under a requirements heading can be copied into a draft and held uncommitted. Model knowledge.
Copying a sentence does not decide that the sentence is an interoperability requirement. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Published means are 13.4, 5.0, 15.2, 40.2 and 26.2. Floors are 13, 5, 15, 40 and 26, which is 99. The extra goes to screens (remainder 0.4), giving 14, 5, 15, 40 and 26.

The spreadsheet floor of 5 is not used. The interface note is a document, not a sheet. Those 5 points move onto documents, so the steps use screens 14, spreadsheet 0, mail 15, documents 45 and meetings 26.
The prior that this work is an integration is refused. The task identifies and records requirements. It does not build the interface.
The actor on every step, including the draft, is the web administrator, because that person writes these requirement sentences today. The machine is only the future fate of the draft.
The structured input is sentences already under a requirements heading in the interface note. The producer is the note read. If the heading is missing, the draft is empty and the record does not run.

Colleague mail and the developer discussion happen before acceptance. They are internal and they do not record the requirements. The identification compares meaning and outputs accepted interoperability requirements v1. It does not edit the draft. A later edit voids that acceptance. The record binds that version and does not change it.
No focal upkeep is added. Identification keeps its full time. One system hour keeps the heading map current. The note does not log who viewed the interface and does not rate staff.
unknowns: Which two systems the interface is expected to join.
Whether the current interface note already uses a requirements heading.
research_questions: Which sentence patterns the interface note uses for a requirement, beyond a heading.
Who else must accept a requirement before it is recorded.

already_counted.description: Judging which copied sentences are real interoperability requirements.

incremental.description: Keep the map from the requirements heading to drafted sentences current when the note template changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the requirements heading is missing, so nothing is drafted. High is 6 when the heading is present and the administrator rejects some sentences. The live read, the mail, the discussion, the identification, and the record stay at full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop or implement ongoing revision procedures.

steps.what: Read the live page state under revision
Read the current revision notes
Draft ongoing revision procedures from the notes
Meet colleagues about ongoing revision exceptions
Check drafted revision procedures for meaning
Develop accepted revision procedures into the record
Mail the team the accepted revision procedures
Implement accepted revision procedures on the public site

tasks.design: The web administrator reads live page state in the {CMS} and revision notes in {DOCS}. A deterministic copy drafts procedure sentences already under the procedure heading and holds them. The meeting about exceptions stays manual. After acceptance, the administrator writes the procedure in {DOCS}, mails the team from {EMAIL}, and implements it on the public site in the {CMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure sentences were typed into the record by hand, and a live page could be changed before the procedure was accepted.
tasks.enabler_now: The revision notes already hold sentences under a procedure heading, so those sentences can be copied and held until a person accepts them.
tasks.still_hard: Only the administrator can accept the procedure. The public implement stays with that person, because an unattended change to a live site is refused.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator checks the drafted sentences against the exceptions and the live page, and is the person who changes the public site.

ambition.what: Accept or refuse a revision procedure for each batch of page changes, not only at a redesign.

tasks.altitude: Less time copying procedure sentences out of the revision notes. The same time on the meeting, the check, the record, the team mail, and the public implement. No new right to change a live page.

reach.task: Hold a change to a live system until a person has accepted the procedure.
reach.learn: A procedure draft is not a deployment, and an unattended change to production is refused.

evidence.claim: Sentences already under a procedure heading can be copied into a draft and held until a person accepts them. Model knowledge.
An unattended agent deleted a production database despite instructions.

assumptions: Published means are 16.4, 7.1, 14.9, 43.0 and 18.6. Floors are 16, 7, 14, 43 and 18, which is 98. Extras go to mail (remainder 0.9) then meetings (remainder 0.6), giving 16, 7, 15, 43 and 19.

The spreadsheet floor of 7 is not used. The revision notes are a document, not a sheet. Those 7 points move onto documents, so the steps use screens 16, spreadsheet 0, mail 15, documents 50 and meetings 19.

The actor on every step, including the draft, is the web administrator, because that person writes the procedure sentences today. The machine is only the future fate of the draft. The draft copies sentences and does not write code.

The structured input is sentences already under a procedure heading in the revision notes. The producer is the notes read. If the heading is missing, the draft is empty and the record, the mail, and the public implement do not run.

The meeting about exceptions happens before the check and does not accept the procedure. The check compares meaning and outputs accepted revision procedure v1. It does not edit the draft. A later edit voids that acceptance.

The record, the team mail, and the public implement each bind that version and do not edit it. The team mail stays inside the organisation. The public implement is done by the administrator and is not an unattended deploy. The procedure does not log editor identity and does not rate staff, so staff-monitoring rules are not opened. A normal revision procedure is not a national cybersecurity duty and not a product-security duty.
No focal upkeep is added. The check keeps its full time. One system hour keeps the heading map current.
unknowns: Who may change the public site when the administrator is away.
Whether the current revision notes already use a procedure heading.
research_questions: Which sentences a revision procedure must contain before it can be accepted.
Whether a second person must accept a change to the public home page.

already_counted.description: Checking drafted procedure sentences against the exceptions and the live page.

incremental.description: Keep the map from the procedure heading to drafted sentences current when the notes template changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is zero when the procedure heading is missing, so nothing is drafted. High is 9 when the heading is present and the check refuses some sentences. The meeting, the check, the record, the team mail, and the public implement stay at full time.
